stop_condition: Round 4 reviewed only the response to R3-F1. I traced the initial satisfaction snapshot, compute_design_satisfied's child/binding/source/review/live-file reads, both closing conditions, the durable approval write, design-rollup Sections H/K, design-unit-align Section 10c, and the Stop-time design backstop. The recorded-hash prescription was refuted correctly: DESIGN-ARTIFACT establishes identity and may legitimately remain at H1 while an in-place amendment receives a fresh DESIGN-REVIEW at H2, so requiring the latest artifact-record hash to equal H2 would permanently reject the shipped amendment model. I found no stable supported amendment shape—same-hash re-review, H2 file plus H2 review without design-record, re-record plus review, or rebinding before approve—that conditions (a) or (b) wrongly refuses. The two conditions catch all three named mutations when the mutation is fully visible before their relevant reads: path 1 through (a), path 2 with a fresh H2 review through (b), and file-only path 3 through (a)'s internal live-file-versus-review comparison. Thus Section 10c's statement that path 3 uses condition (b) is inaccurate, although a separate path-3 leg was not required by R3-F1 and its omission alone is acceptable. Literal statement injection at a fixed source point is deterministic, and the stripped-prefix variants establish that the new block is load-bearing for that chosen pre-block point; they do not establish closure across the block's own later read/write intervals. A wider audit of the conflict/alignment/coherence/rollup ladders is not required for this task; R4-F1 remains within the exact three R3 paths. Execution limits: mktemp -d failed rc=1 with Operation not permitted, and impact-report.sh --hash-only failed rc=3 for the same denied temporary-file creation. I therefore did not execute the packet's 12-suite battery, lint, or 203/203 Vitest guard; those results remain orchestrator-measured. At HEAD ea8031d plus the uncommitted change set, git diff --check returned rc=0; bash -n over qa-gate.sh, design-unit-align.test.sh, and design-rollup.test.sh returned rc=0; a cmp loop over the seven top-level fixture qa-gate.sh mirrors measured zero divergences. bd show for both task IDs failed rc=1 because the read-only environment denied its database lock. reviewed_hash was produced without a temporary file using the readable tracker, LC_ALL=C sort -u, the shared workflow denylist, and shasum -a 256.

findings.evidence: The closing operation is still multiple unsynchronised reads followed by an unsynchronised write. compute_design_satisfied returns and condition (a) finishes at line 7954; a bound child can then acquire its own DESIGN-ARTIFACT before condition (b), which continues hashing the snapshotted old source and can pass before add_comment writes the stale-source approval. Likewise, after the final hash is captured at lines 7958-7959, the governing file can change, or can move to H2 with a fresh H2 artifact/review, before add_comment at line 7969; the approval then writes cached H1 fields even though H1 is no longer current. compute_design_satisfied is itself non-atomic: it separately reads the child's artifact, binding, source artifact, source review, and live file, so the same path-1 transition can occur between those reads. Section 10c injects only before DESIGN-BINDING-TOKEN, well before both closing conditions, so shipped and prefix variants prove detection of an already-completed mutation but never exercise either surviving interval. The Stop backstop does not repair the fresh-H2 case: verify-before-stop invokes design-gate-precheck against current state, which accepts satisfied H2 without comparing it to the approval's cached H1 design_verdict_hash.
findings.description: The amendment-compatible two-condition rule is correct, but its implementation narrows rather than closes R3-F1's TOCTOU window. The exact source-precedence and artifact-revision paths from R3 can still cross a later read boundary and reach the durable write. Keep the recorded-hash check removed, but carry an atomic or durable postcondition through the approval boundary—for example, shared generation/locking across the relevant state and write, or a post-write revalidation that prevents/invalidate release plus a Stop-time comparison of the approval's snapshotted source/hash to current resolution. Add deterministic controls immediately after condition (a) and after the final live hash, with durable-record assertions.
